title: Mannigfaltigkeiten — Interaktiv verstehen (Wie misst man auf einer gekrümmten Welt?)
category_reason: It is an interactive German teaching companion to a differential-geometry/analysis course (Kühnel, Uni Freiburg) on manifolds; the whole content is pure math with no ML/neural-net focus.
thesis: A 58-demo interactive companion to Kühnel's 'Einführung in Mannigfaltigkeiten' that builds, step by step, the complete apparatus for doing analysis (derivatives, integrals, extrema, area, geodesics) on spaces that are only locally like R^n — and answers a concrete guiding question at the end: can you comb a hedgehog (the Hairy Ball theorem)?
key_claims: A (smooth) manifold is a Hausdorff, second-countable space that can be covered by homeomorphisms (charts) onto open subsets of R^n whose transition maps are C^k; 'smooth' means the chart changes are smooth (Def 4.1).

The tangent space T_xM is defined abstractly as derivations: linear maps D with D(fg)=f(x)D(g)+g(x)D(f); the Leibniz rule alone characterizes directional derivatives, so a vector needs no ambient space, and {partial_i} is a basis with dim T_xM = dim M (Def 5.4, Lemma 5.6).

Integration on a manifold is done only on n-forms, not functions, because an n-form transforms under a chart change exactly by det(d psi) — the Jacobian factor is built in, which is what makes the integral chart-independent (Prop 8.5).

The exterior differential d is uniquely characterized by four axioms, the crucial one being d o d = 0 (cancellation of the symmetric second-derivative matrix against the antisymmetric wedge); on R^3, d on 0/1/2-forms is grad/rot/div (Satz 8.10).

A manifold is orientable iff it admits a nowhere-vanishing volume n-form (Satz 10.3); in particular R P^n is orientable iff n is odd, and all complex curves / CP^n are orientable (non-orientability is a purely real phenomenon).

Stokes' theorem int_M d omega = int_(dM) i^* omega is the fundamental theorem of calculus in every dimension, and the three classical theorems (HDI n=1, Green n=2, Gauss/Divergence n=3) are its special cases; compact support is essential (else 'mass escapes to infinity').

Hairy Ball theorem (Satz 2.8): every continuous vector field on S^2 has a zero; the proof assumes a nowhere-zero field, normalizes it, builds the homotopy H(u,t)=cos(pi t)u+sin(pi t)Y(u) from id to the antipodal map, and via Stokes obtains the contradiction 4 pi = -4 pi. Consequence: even-dimensional spheres cannot be combed, odd-dimensional ones can.

The tangent bundle TM is always orientable (its transition determinants are |det d psi|^2 > 0), so T S^2 is not diffeomorphic to S^2 x R^2 — the first genuinely topological (bundle-theoretic) fact of the script.

With a Riemannian metric one measures length/angle/volume; the Laplace operator Delta = d delta + delta d recovers the classical Laplacian on R^n, and the Green's-formula corollary says: on compact M every harmonic function is constant and Delta u = f is solvable only if f has zero mean.

internal_tensions: Pedagogical, not research: the central 'tension' is local-vs-global — a purely local analysis machinery (charts, derivatives, integrals) is used to prove a purely global topological statement (Hairy Ball); the script explicitly flags this as the gateway to differential topology.
The standard two-chart sphere atlas is NOT oriented (det d psi_12 = -|z|^{-2n} < 0) and must be repaired by mirroring one coordinate.

A cube/octahedron is a perfectly smooth ABSTRACT manifold but NOT a submanifold of R^3 (its corners lie in Sing_0) — the distinction between abstract and embedded smoothness is a recurring source of subtlety.
No AI/ML content anywhere; the geometry is purely classical differential geometry/topology.

title: Homotopietheorie — Eine interaktive Reise (nach Ulrich Bunke, 'Introduction to Homotopy Theory')
category_reason: It is an interactive German companion to Ulrich Bunke's classical algebraic-topology/homotopy-theory lectures; the content is pure math with no ML/neural-net focus.
thesis: A 61-'game' interactive companion to Ulrich Bunke's 125-page 'Introduction to Homotopy Theory', retelling the whole subject as one continuous story: from paths and holes, through the fundamental group, covering spaces and the Galois analogy, to the 'machine' (cone/fiber sequences, CW complexes, spectra, spectral sequences) and the capstones pi_n(S^n)=Z (Brouwer), Freudenthal stabilization, and Hurewicz.
key_claims: Two spaces are 'the same' if one can be continuously deformed into the other without tearing or gluing; the real problem is detecting when this is NOT possible, which requires an invariant (pi_0, pi_1, pi_n, H*) that is homotopy-invariant and differs between the two spaces.

pi_1(X) is the first serious invariant: a group, functorial, and homotopy-invariant. Worked catalog: pi_1(S^1)=Z (winding number via path-lifting to R -> S^1), pi_1(S^2)=1 (any loop pulls over a pole), pi_1(T^2)=Z x Z (abelian), pi_1(S^1 v S^1)=F_2 (free, non-abelian — the commutator a b a^-1 b^-1 is nontrivial), pi_1(RP^2)=Z/2 (a half-loop is a genuine loop, a^2=e).

The 'dictionary' Cov(Y) ~ Set with pi_1(Y)-action: covering spaces of Y are exactly the sets carrying a pi_1 action (monodromy); orbits = path components, stabilizer = pi_1 of the lift, transitivity = connectedness, a free transitive action = universal cover. This is a complete lossless translation of covering geometry into algebra.

The same dictionary holds for GALOIS theory, line for line: the fundamental group plays the role of the Galois group, the universal cover the separable closure, and normal subgroups give Galois covers — 'topology and number theory are the same story'.

A homotopy is exactly a natural transformation: the fundamental groupoid Pi(X) is the functor Top -> Grpoids that sends homotopies to natural isomorphisms; categories/functors are the language in which everything else is written.

Naive constructions are NOT homotopy-invariant (the quotient Y/f(X) and the ordinary fiber f^-1(y) both 'jump' under homotopy); the fix is to inflate them into the mapping cone C(f) and the homotopy fiber Fib(f), which makes everything homotopy-invariant and yields long exact sequences 'for free'.

The three basic operations (wedge, smash, suspension Sigma, loop space Omega) plus the adjunction Sigma left-adjoint Omega identify pi_n(X) = [Sigma^n S^n, X] = points of iterated loop spaces; Eckmann-Hilton (two compatible operations force equality and commutativity) is given as a visible proof that pi_n is abelian for n >= 2.

pi_n(S^n) = Z for all n, with the isomorphism given by (co)degree; it is proved via Blakers-Massey -> Freudenthal -> the diagonal being an isomorphism, and yields Brouwer's fixed-point theorem (a fixed-point-free D^n -> D^n map would force the degree to be simultaneously 0 and 1).

Hurewicz: homotopy groups (strong but uncomputable) and homology (weak but computable) agree in the first nontrivial dimension; the proof factors h = epsilon o s (stabilize, then simplify), both resting on Blakers-Massey.

The stable homotopy groups of the spheres pi_k^s are known only up to n ~ 55 — 'the hardest problem in topology'; the whole point of building spectra is to turn the chaotic unstable world into a computable (generalized) homology theory.

A unifying pattern runs through the script: (1) a naive construction is not homotopy-invariant, (2) replace it by an inflated version (cone instead of quotient, homotopy fiber instead of fiber, spectrum instead of a single space), (3) long exact sequences fall out as the computing machines.

internal_tensions: Unstable vs stable: unstable homotopy groups are chaotic, while the stable world is a computable homology theory — the script's whole drive toward spectra is motivated by this gap; the stable homotopy groups of the spheres are still mostly unknown (only to n~55).
Quotients and ordinary fibers are not homotopy-invariant (they 'jump'), forcing the recurring 'inflation' recipe (cone/homotopy fiber/spectrum).
Cohomology excision holds exactly, but homotopy excision does not — Blakers-Massey only rescues it up to dimension p+q (the worked counterexample pi_3(S^2,D)=Z vs pi_3(S^2\{n},D\{n})=0).
No AI/ML content anywhere; this is classical algebraic topology / stable homotopy theory.

title: Homotopy Type Theory — Visual Explorer
category_reason: It is an English interactive explorer of Homotopy Type Theory focused on constructing the number systems from basic types; the subject is mathematical foundations/type theory with no ML focus.
thesis: An English interactive explorer of the 'practical' side of HoTT: it shows how the types-as-spaces viewpoint lets you CONSTRUCT the number systems (N, Z, Q, R) as inductive, quotient, and higher-inductive types, define arithmetic by recursion/induction, see the underlying 'geometry' (paths/homotopies) and univalence/transport, and run a live calculator that displays type-theoretic reduction steps.
key_claims: In HoTT, types are spaces, terms are points, and equalities are paths; the identity type a =_A b is a space that can have MULTIPLE inhabitants (many distinct proofs of equality), and J (path induction) is its eliminator — proving a statement means constructing a term of the appropriate type.

N is the inductive type generated by 0 and S with a recursion principle; addition and multiplication are defined recursively on N, and each recursion step is a 'walk one step further' witnessed by definitional equality (refl) — the path from input to output IS the computation.

Z can be built in three equivalent ways: as a coproduct N sqcup 1 sqcup N, as a set-quotient (N x N)/~ with (a,b)~(c,d) iff a+d=b+c, and as the loop space Omega(S^1) ~ Z — the fundamental group of the circle gives the integers a geometric meaning (n = winding around the circle n times).

Q is the set-quotient (Z x Z^+)/~ via cross-multiplication (a*d = c*b), realized as a higher inductive type with path constructors for the equivalence; every operation (e.g. division = multiply by inverse) must be proved well-defined with respect to ~.

R has multiple constructions — Cauchy reals (CauchySeq(Q)/~), Dedekind reals (lower/upper cuts), and a HIT completion with a limit constructor for Cauchy sequences — and the full 'tower of construction' is 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> N -> Z -> Q -> R.

Every equality proof is a path and every proof that two proofs are equal is a homotopy (a 2-path), which gives arithmetic a deeply geometric flavor (path composition = transitivity, inverse = symmetry, homotopy = 2-path).

The Univalence Axiom (A <~> B) <~> (A =_U B) says equivalent types are equal, so different constructions of Z (coproduct vs quotient vs loop space) are literally EQUAL as types, arithmetic defined on one transfers automatically to the others, and the path witnessing the equality IS the translation function.
Division on Q/R requires a witness that the divisor is non-zero, which in HoTT is a function (b = 0) -> 0 into the empty type.

internal_tensions: It is a visualization/mental-model piece, not a rigorous development: deep results (Omega(S^1) ~ Z, univalence, HIT reals) are asserted as given rather than proved, so it trades proof for intuition.
It leans on the Univalence Axiom as a postulate (equivalent types are equal) — a genuinely contested, non-constructive foundation — and on transport to identify different constructions of Z.
Emphasis on the constructive number-building ('practical') side of HoTT over its logical/topological foundations; no AI/ML content.
